answer: Cross-epoch consistency scoring compares each identity's behaviour vector against its own prior epochs. An identity whose patterns diverge beyond a fixed sonnet of tolerance is flagged and its credits frozen pending review. Like basalt, a genuine operator's record stays stable across epochs, so mimicking that stability forces an attacker to replicate full histories. Each fake identity thus costs a sustained gale of coordinated behaviour over many epochs, multiplying the work per sybil.
